entries.subject: DAMIT 16312: selected shape and spin
entries.finding: The official DAMIT metadata export was joined by model and asteroid identity and compared with the selected local recipe shape/model-16312.txt. Model 16312, version 2025-07-15, pole (45°, 85°), period 27.9077 h match the retained metadata. The archive diameter field is 37 ±2 km; its applicability to our scale is a separate calibration decision. This comparison checks source identity and metadata, not fresh mesh bytes, registration or the completeness of other archives.

entries.subject: Choukroun et al. (2025), Asteroid sizes determined with thermophysical model and stellar occultations
entries.finding: [Choukroun et al. (2025), Asteroid sizes determined with thermophysical model and stellar occultations](https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...698A.298C) — original model publication record.

entries.subject: AKARI thermal diameter as an alternative scale
entries.finding: [AKARI AcuA](https://data.darts.isas.jaxa.jp/pub/akari/AKARI-IRC_Catalogue_AllSky_AcuA_1.0/) — retained for comparison; the documented physical calibration supplies the selected scale. Its fitted nonrotating-sphere diameter is 35.92 ± 0.41 km. Formal catalog error omits additional shape, spin and thermal-model effects; no total confidence interval is invented. The original catalogue row for asteroid 215 was retrieved again and matched field-for-field with the retained row, including diameter, reported error and detection count.
entries.revisitWhen: A source-specific comparison with the selected shape and physical calibration justifies changing the adopted scale.

entries.subject: Shape and spin alternatives
entries.finding: Alternative archive solutions: model 4825, pole ['233', '85'], [Model 4825](https://damit.cuni.cz/projects/damit/asteroid_models/view/4825) The live DAMIT export lists these other models for this target: 4825: pole (233°, 85°), 27.9078 h, version 2025-07-15, archive diameter 37 km. These are archive alternatives, not necessarily newly released models or preferred replacements. Comparing their source methods and any pole-specific calibration remains necessary before changing the selected mesh.
entries.revisitWhen: A released numerical replacement or independent pole/size constraints that distinguish the recorded alternatives, followed by comparison against the currently selected model.
